column6: The original paragraph refers to Zachariah as a 'living testament,' while the back-translation describes him as a 'living testimony.' This subtle shift in wording may imply a difference in the emphasis on the nature of his existence as a representation of God's faithfulness, which can affect the doctrinal interpretation of his role.
